title: Transforming Li<sub>3</sub>PS<sub>4</sub> Via Halide Incorporation: a Path to Improved Ionic Conductivity and Stability in All‐Solid‐State Batteries

abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>To enhance Li<jats:sup>+</jats:sup> transport in all‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs), harnessing localized nanoscale disorder can be instrumental, especially in sulfide‐based solid electrolytes (SEs). In this investigation, the transformation of the model SE, Li<jats:sub>3</jats:sub>PS<jats:sub>4</jats:sub>, is delved into via the introduction of LiBr. <jats:sup>31</jats:sup>P nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR)unveils the emergence of a glassy PS<jats:sub>4</jats:sub><jats:sup>3−</jats:sup> network interspersed with Br<jats:sup>−</jats:sup>. <jats:sup>6</jats:sup>Li NMR corroborates swift Li<jats:sup>+</jats:sup> migration between PS<jats:sub>4</jats:sub><jats:sup>3−</jats:sup> and Br<jats:sup>−</jats:sup>, with increased Li<jats:sup>+</jats:sup> mobility indicated by NMR relaxation measurements. A more than fourfold enhancement in ionic conductivity is observed upon LiBr incorporation into Li<jats:sub>3</jats:sub>PS<jats:sub>4</jats:sub>. Moreover, a notable decrease in activation energy underscores the pivotal role of Br<jats:sup>−</jats:sup> incorporation within the anionic lattice, effectively reducing the energy barrier for ion conduction and transitioning Li<jats:sup>+</jats:sup> transport dimensionality from 2D to 3D. The compatibility of Li<jats:sub>3</jats:sub>PS<jats:sub>4</jats:sub> with Li metal is improved through LiBr incorporation, alongside an increase in critical current density from 0.34 to 0.50 mA cm<jats:sup>−2</jats:sup>, while preserving the electrochemical stability window. ASSBs with 3Li<jats:sub>3</jats:sub>PS<jats:sub>4</jats:sub>:LiBr as the SE  showcase robust high‐rate and long‐term cycling performance. These findings collectively indicate the potential of lithium halide incorporation as a promising avenue to enhance the ionic conductivity and stability of SEs.</jats:p>
